topic.title: Converse: hands-free voice
topic.shortdesc: Talk to Command Centre instead of typing: hear what's new, go through approvals and ask for things, with one big button or none at all. Made for the car.

image.alt: Converse on a phone: the chat box grown to fill the screen, with Read aloud, Fold and the Push to talk switch along the top, a large Talk orb in the middle, and who you are talking to at the bottom.

body.p: Tap Converse in the Chat box. The box grows to fill the screen and the talk orb fades in, in the middle of it. Its own controls stay where they were: Read aloud at the top, beside Push to talk, and the text box, Send and the rest at the bottom. Fold, in the place of Converse, folds it back to typing. On a touch screen you can also swipe up on the strip down the right-hand edge of the Chat box to open it, and swipe down on the same strip to fold it.

The screen stays awake while it's open, and after the first tap a headset or steering-wheel play/pause button works as the orb. The microphone stays on while it's open too (the browser shows that it's in use), so each turn starts straight away without losing your first words; folding it away turns the microphone off.
On a computer, Space works as the orb, unless you're typing in the text box: hold it to talk and let go to send, or tap it to start and again to send. While it speaks, Space interrupts.

Push to talk is off to start with: tap Talk once, then speak and pause, and it listens again after each answer. Turn it on to tap Talk, speak, and tap Send each time. Each device remembers your choice.

While it speaks, the orb says Interrupt. The picker at the bottom, where Chat has Send to, chooses who you are talking to: the default, Assistant, which works across all your businesses, or one of the specialists. You can also type a command in the text box and press Send. What you ask and the answers go in the Chat's log too, marked with a microphone, so they're kept with the rest of the day's chat.

Small talk and quick questions get an answer straight away; anything about your businesses, or anything to do, goes to the agents, and their answer is spoken when it comes. Talk on from it as you would to a person: a follow-up such as yes, send it, no, the other one or and when will it arrive? goes back to the same task, which carries on from what it already found (or takes it as soon as it finishes, if it's still working). Something new starts a new task. A follow-up counts for about 20 minutes after the answer.
In Settings, under Converse, you can turn on Listen for a follow-up after each answer and choose what the orb shows. The voice it speaks with is under Voice.
body.note: Approvals by voice always ask you to confirm: say approve, hear what it is, then say yes, approve. A request such as approve the quote for Jane is sent to the agent as a request, never taken as an approval.

body.p: A command must be the whole thing you say. OK, hey, please and thanks around it are fine. Anything else is sent to the agent as a request.

strow.stentry: what's new, brief me, catch me up
Go through what needs your approval, one at a time.
Start approving or rejecting the one just read. It reads it back and asks you to confirm.
Turn push to talk on or off.
talk to the video producer, back to the assistant
Choose who you are talking to.

body.p: To send one request to a business or a specialist, start with its name: shop: has order 1042 shipped? or ask the blog writer to draft the build log. Spoken names work: d m s or machine shop, three d p and me, open v, open d, personal.
When the agent asks you a question, whatever you say next is your answer; only stop, cancel, end, repeat and the mode switches still work as commands.

The orb shows a live trace of your voice while you speak and of the reply while it is spoken, sweeping round it. Under Show in Settings → Converse you can keep both, or choose the orb only or the trace only.
